readings.title: A Rainy Sunday
readings.desc: 一个安静的雨天，一段温暖的小故事
text: Last Sunday, it rained all day. Anna decided to stay at home and read her favorite book. She made a cup of hot tea and sat by the window. The rain sang a soft song on the roof, and the whole city became quiet.

While she was reading, her cat jumped onto her legs and fell asleep. Anna smiled and touched its warm back. She thought about her grandmother, who taught her how to make bread on rainy days. The kitchen smelled wonderful when the bread was ready.

In the afternoon, the rain stopped. Anna opened the window and took a deep breath. The air was fresh and clean. Birds started to sing in the garden again. She picked up her phone and called her best friend. They talked and laughed for two hours.
It was a simple day, but Anna felt happy. Sometimes, a quiet day at home is the best gift.

readings.title: The Bookshop on Green Street
readings.desc: 街角书店与守门人的故事
text: At the corner of Green Street, there is a small bookshop. It has been there for thirty years. The owner, Mr. Carter, is an elderly man with white hair and round glasses. He knows every book on his shelves.

Every Saturday morning, students visit the shop to find stories for the weekend. Mr. Carter always recommends the right book. 'This one is about a boy who sails across the ocean,' he says with a smile. 'You will love the adventure.'

Last week, I asked him why he never sold the shop. He cleaned his glasses slowly and thought for a moment. 'Books are like doors,' he answered. 'Each one opens into a different world. I am just the man who keeps the doors open.'

I bought a mystery novel that afternoon. When I read the first page at home, I could not stop. Outside, the city was noisy, but inside my room, everything was silent. Somewhere in the story, a ship was crossing the dark sea, and I was on it.

readings.title: Why Do We Dream?
readings.desc: 科学家如何解释奇妙的梦境
text: Every night, when you close your eyes, your brain begins a strange journey. You may fly over mountains, talk with old friends, or suddenly find yourself late for an exam. These experiences are called dreams, and scientists are still trying to understand them.

One famous theory says that dreams help the brain organize memories. During the day, we receive millions of pieces of information. At night, the brain sorts them, keeping what is important and throwing away the rest. This is why students who sleep well often remember lessons better.
Another theory connects dreams with emotions. When you feel worried, you may dream about failing a test. The dream gives your mind a safe place to face its fears.

Modern research uses machines that watch the sleeping brain. In one experiment, scientists woke people up during a special stage of sleep and asked them to describe their dreams. The results suggest that most dreams are about the people and problems from our daily lives.
So tonight, before you close your eyes, remember: your brain is going to work.

readings.title: A Letter from Grandma
readings.desc: 一封来自外婆的信，朴素而温暖
text: Dear Lily, thank you for your email. I was so happy to hear from you. Your grandfather and I are both well. The weather in the village is getting cool, and the trees are turning yellow.
This week I picked many apples from our garden. They are small but very sweet. I made two bottles of apple jam for you. I will send them with Uncle Wang when he goes to the city next week.

Your grandfather asks about your English study every day. He tells everyone in the village that his granddaughter can talk with foreigners. We are so proud of you. Study hard, but also sleep early and eat well.
Come back for the winter holiday. Grandma will make your favorite dumplings. With all my love, Grandma.

readings.title: The Power of Reading
readings.desc: 为什么阅读是最划算的自我投资
text: If you could buy one hour of a great writer's life for the price of a cup of coffee, would you do it? In fact, you do it every time you open a book. A writer may spend ten years thinking about a problem, and you can receive the answer in a single afternoon.

Reading is also a form of quiet conversation. When you read, you hear the thoughts of people who lived hundreds of years ago, or who live on the other side of the earth. Their experience becomes part of your memory, and their mistakes become your lessons.

Scientists have found that regular reading does more than fill the brain with facts. It trains attention, because you must follow an idea for many pages. It also builds the habit of patience, which is rare in a world of short videos.

You do not need to read fast, and you do not need to read everything. Choose books that truly interest you, read them slowly, and talk about them with friends. A few good books, read with care, can change the way you see the world.

readings.title: A Rainy Sunday
readings.desc: 一个安静的雨天，一段温暖的小故事
text: Last Sunday, it rained all day. Anna decided to stay at home and read her favorite book. She made a cup of hot tea and sat by the window. The rain sang a soft song on the roof, and the whole city became quiet.

While she was reading, her cat jumped onto her legs and fell asleep. Anna smiled and touched its warm back. She thought about her grandmother, who taught her how to make bread on rainy days. The kitchen smelled wonderful when the bread was ready.

In the afternoon, the rain stopped. Anna opened the window and took a deep breath. The air was fresh and clean. Birds started to sing in the garden again. She picked up her phone and called her best friend. They talked and laughed for two hours.
It was a simple day, but Anna felt happy. Sometimes, a quiet day at home is the best gift.

readings.title: The Bookshop on Green Street
readings.desc: 街角书店与守门人的故事
text: At the corner of Green Street, there is a small bookshop. It has been there for thirty years. The owner, Mr. Carter, is an elderly man with white hair and round glasses. He knows every book on his shelves.

Every Saturday morning, students visit the shop to find stories for the weekend. Mr. Carter always recommends the right book. 'This one is about a boy who sails across the ocean,' he says with a smile. 'You will love the adventure.'

Last week, I asked him why he never sold the shop. He cleaned his glasses slowly and thought for a moment. 'Books are like doors,' he answered. 'Each one opens into a different world. I am just the man who keeps the doors open.'

I bought a mystery novel that afternoon. When I read the first page at home, I could not stop. Outside, the city was noisy, but inside my room, everything was silent. Somewhere in the story, a ship was crossing the dark sea, and I was on it.

readings.title: Why Do We Dream?
readings.desc: 科学家如何解释奇妙的梦境
text: Every night, when you close your eyes, your brain begins a strange journey. You may fly over mountains, talk with old friends, or suddenly find yourself late for an exam. These experiences are called dreams, and scientists are still trying to understand them.

One famous theory says that dreams help the brain organize memories. During the day, we receive millions of pieces of information. At night, the brain sorts them, keeping what is important and throwing away the rest. This is why students who sleep well often remember lessons better.
Another theory connects dreams with emotions. When you feel worried, you may dream about failing a test. The dream gives your mind a safe place to face its fears.

Modern research uses machines that watch the sleeping brain. In one experiment, scientists woke people up during a special stage of sleep and asked them to describe their dreams. The results suggest that most dreams are about the people and problems from our daily lives.
So tonight, before you close your eyes, remember: your brain is going to work.

readings.title: A Letter from Grandma
readings.desc: 一封来自外婆的信，朴素而温暖
text: Dear Lily, thank you for your email. I was so happy to hear from you. Your grandfather and I are both well. The weather in the village is getting cool, and the trees are turning yellow.
This week I picked many apples from our garden. They are small but very sweet. I made two bottles of apple jam for you. I will send them with Uncle Wang when he goes to the city next week.

Your grandfather asks about your English study every day. He tells everyone in the village that his granddaughter can talk with foreigners. We are so proud of you. Study hard, but also sleep early and eat well.
Come back for the winter holiday. Grandma will make your favorite dumplings. With all my love, Grandma.

readings.title: The Power of Reading
readings.desc: 为什么阅读是最划算的自我投资
text: If you could buy one hour of a great writer's life for the price of a cup of coffee, would you do it? In fact, you do it every time you open a book. A writer may spend ten years thinking about a problem, and you can receive the answer in a single afternoon.

Reading is also a form of quiet conversation. When you read, you hear the thoughts of people who lived hundreds of years ago, or who live on the other side of the earth. Their experience becomes part of your memory, and their mistakes become your lessons.

Scientists have found that regular reading does more than fill the brain with facts. It trains attention, because you must follow an idea for many pages. It also builds the habit of patience, which is rare in a world of short videos.

You do not need to read fast, and you do not need to read everything. Choose books that truly interest you, read them slowly, and talk about them with friends. A few good books, read with care, can change the way you see the world.

readings.title: A Rainy Sunday
readings.desc: 一个安静的雨天，一段温暖的小故事
text: Last Sunday, it rained all day. Anna decided to stay at home and read her favorite book. She made a cup of hot tea and sat by the window. The rain sang a soft song on the roof, and the whole city became quiet.

While she was reading, her cat jumped onto her legs and fell asleep. Anna smiled and touched its warm back. She thought about her grandmother, who taught her how to make bread on rainy days. The kitchen smelled wonderful when the bread was ready.

In the afternoon, the rain stopped. Anna opened the window and took a deep breath. The air was fresh and clean. Birds started to sing in the garden again. She picked up her phone and called her best friend. They talked and laughed for two hours.
It was a simple day, but Anna felt happy. Sometimes, a quiet day at home is the best gift.

readings.title: The Bookshop on Green Street
readings.desc: 街角书店与守门人的故事
text: At the corner of Green Street, there is a small bookshop. It has been there for thirty years. The owner, Mr. Carter, is an elderly man with white hair and round glasses. He knows every book on his shelves.

Every Saturday morning, students visit the shop to find stories for the weekend. Mr. Carter always recommends the right book. 'This one is about a boy who sails across the ocean,' he says with a smile. 'You will love the adventure.'

Last week, I asked him why he never sold the shop. He cleaned his glasses slowly and thought for a moment. 'Books are like doors,' he answered. 'Each one opens into a different world. I am just the man who keeps the doors open.'

I bought a mystery novel that afternoon. When I read the first page at home, I could not stop. Outside, the city was noisy, but inside my room, everything was silent. Somewhere in the story, a ship was crossing the dark sea, and I was on it.

readings.title: Why Do We Dream?
readings.desc: 科学家如何解释奇妙的梦境
text: Every night, when you close your eyes, your brain begins a strange journey. You may fly over mountains, talk with old friends, or suddenly find yourself late for an exam. These experiences are called dreams, and scientists are still trying to understand them.

One famous theory says that dreams help the brain organize memories. During the day, we receive millions of pieces of information. At night, the brain sorts them, keeping what is important and throwing away the rest. This is why students who sleep well often remember lessons better.
Another theory connects dreams with emotions. When you feel worried, you may dream about failing a test. The dream gives your mind a safe place to face its fears.

Modern research uses machines that watch the sleeping brain. In one experiment, scientists woke people up during a special stage of sleep and asked them to describe their dreams. The results suggest that most dreams are about the people and problems from our daily lives.
So tonight, before you close your eyes, remember: your brain is going to work.

readings.title: A Letter from Grandma
readings.desc: 一封来自外婆的信，朴素而温暖
text: Dear Lily, thank you for your email. I was so happy to hear from you. Your grandfather and I are both well. The weather in the village is getting cool, and the trees are turning yellow.
This week I picked many apples from our garden. They are small but very sweet. I made two bottles of apple jam for you. I will send them with Uncle Wang when he goes to the city next week.

Your grandfather asks about your English study every day. He tells everyone in the village that his granddaughter can talk with foreigners. We are so proud of you. Study hard, but also sleep early and eat well.
Come back for the winter holiday. Grandma will make your favorite dumplings. With all my love, Grandma.

readings.title: The Power of Reading
readings.desc: 为什么阅读是最划算的自我投资
text: If you could buy one hour of a great writer's life for the price of a cup of coffee, would you do it? In fact, you do it every time you open a book. A writer may spend ten years thinking about a problem, and you can receive the answer in a single afternoon.

Reading is also a form of quiet conversation. When you read, you hear the thoughts of people who lived hundreds of years ago, or who live on the other side of the earth. Their experience becomes part of your memory, and their mistakes become your lessons.

Scientists have found that regular reading does more than fill the brain with facts. It trains attention, because you must follow an idea for many pages. It also builds the habit of patience, which is rare in a world of short videos.

You do not need to read fast, and you do not need to read everything. Choose books that truly interest you, read them slowly, and talk about them with friends. A few good books, read with care, can change the way you see the world.

readings.title: A Rainy Sunday
readings.desc: 一个安静的雨天，一段温暖的小故事
text: Last Sunday, it rained all day. Anna decided to stay at home and read her favorite book. She made a cup of hot tea and sat by the window. The rain sang a soft song on the roof, and the whole city became quiet.

While she was reading, her cat jumped onto her legs and fell asleep. Anna smiled and touched its warm back. She thought about her grandmother, who taught her how to make bread on rainy days. The kitchen smelled wonderful when the bread was ready.

In the afternoon, the rain stopped. Anna opened the window and took a deep breath. The air was fresh and clean. Birds started to sing in the garden again. She picked up her phone and called her best friend. They talked and laughed for two hours.
It was a simple day, but Anna felt happy. Sometimes, a quiet day at home is the best gift.

readings.title: The Bookshop on Green Street
readings.desc: 街角书店与守门人的故事
text: At the corner of Green Street, there is a small bookshop. It has been there for thirty years. The owner, Mr. Carter, is an elderly man with white hair and round glasses. He knows every book on his shelves.

Every Saturday morning, students visit the shop to find stories for the weekend. Mr. Carter always recommends the right book. 'This one is about a boy who sails across the ocean,' he says with a smile. 'You will love the adventure.'

Last week, I asked him why he never sold the shop. He cleaned his glasses slowly and thought for a moment. 'Books are like doors,' he answered. 'Each one opens into a different world. I am just the man who keeps the doors open.'

I bought a mystery novel that afternoon. When I read the first page at home, I could not stop. Outside, the city was noisy, but inside my room, everything was silent. Somewhere in the story, a ship was crossing the dark sea, and I was on it.

readings.title: Why Do We Dream?
readings.desc: 科学家如何解释奇妙的梦境
text: Every night, when you close your eyes, your brain begins a strange journey. You may fly over mountains, talk with old friends, or suddenly find yourself late for an exam. These experiences are called dreams, and scientists are still trying to understand them.

One famous theory says that dreams help the brain organize memories. During the day, we receive millions of pieces of information. At night, the brain sorts them, keeping what is important and throwing away the rest. This is why students who sleep well often remember lessons better.
Another theory connects dreams with emotions. When you feel worried, you may dream about failing a test. The dream gives your mind a safe place to face its fears.

Modern research uses machines that watch the sleeping brain. In one experiment, scientists woke people up during a special stage of sleep and asked them to describe their dreams. The results suggest that most dreams are about the people and problems from our daily lives.
So tonight, before you close your eyes, remember: your brain is going to work.

readings.title: A Letter from Grandma
readings.desc: 一封来自外婆的信，朴素而温暖
text: Dear Lily, thank you for your email. I was so happy to hear from you. Your grandfather and I are both well. The weather in the village is getting cool, and the trees are turning yellow.
This week I picked many apples from our garden. They are small but very sweet. I made two bottles of apple jam for you. I will send them with Uncle Wang when he goes to the city next week.

Your grandfather asks about your English study every day. He tells everyone in the village that his granddaughter can talk with foreigners. We are so proud of you. Study hard, but also sleep early and eat well.
Come back for the winter holiday. Grandma will make your favorite dumplings. With all my love, Grandma.

readings.title: The Power of Reading
readings.desc: 为什么阅读是最划算的自我投资
text: If you could buy one hour of a great writer's life for the price of a cup of coffee, would you do it? In fact, you do it every time you open a book. A writer may spend ten years thinking about a problem, and you can receive the answer in a single afternoon.

Reading is also a form of quiet conversation. When you read, you hear the thoughts of people who lived hundreds of years ago, or who live on the other side of the earth. Their experience becomes part of your memory, and their mistakes become your lessons.

Scientists have found that regular reading does more than fill the brain with facts. It trains attention, because you must follow an idea for many pages. It also builds the habit of patience, which is rare in a world of short videos.

You do not need to read fast, and you do not need to read everything. Choose books that truly interest you, read them slowly, and talk about them with friends. A few good books, read with care, can change the way you see the world.
